title: POC Weekly - traffic shaping & fallback experiments
summary: Weekly pilot sync to review traffic-shaping experiments and fallback routing results on the BlueCrest Private pilot. Discussed kernel upgrade impact on p95 latency, intermittent egress failures, and next steps for a larger load test and security artifact handoff.
action_items: Jordan Kim — share secure-architecture diagram + gated KMS notes — 2025-10-10
Marta Ruiz — run focused p95 bench with kernel rollback (v1.2.4 -> v1.2.3) and share csv — 2025-10-09
Marcus Leung — provide full egress ACLs and current NAT gateway metrics — 2025-10-08
Priya Shah — confirm compliance contact for SOC2 artifacts and whether BlueCrest legal needs additional DPA clauses — 2025-10-13
next_steps: Schedule 60m deep-dive for kernel regression if Marta sees >8% p95 regression
Execute 10k-request load burst with prefix caching enabled and compare token-cost delta
Redwood to provision temporary dedicated pool for weekend soak test (2x medium gpus)
Exchange SAML metadata + test user for SSO staging
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-07 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim, Marta Ruiz, Noah Green (Redwood) — Priya Shah, Marcus Leung, Ellen Park (BlueCrest)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check in — we have about 50 minutes. Couple things on the agenda: traffic shaping results from last week's experiment, the fallback routing we rolled out, and the kernel upgrade impact Marta flagged. Also any security asks from BlueCrest.

[00:28] Priya Shah: Thanks Jordan. We'll start with a quick rundown of what we saw on our side. So after enabling the fallback routing, we observed fewer hard failures but saw an odd spike in p95 for longer prompts around 2:30am last thursday, unclear whether that's routing or local resource contention.

[00:55] Marta Ruiz: Right, we saw that on our telemetry too. The spike correlates with a burst where the KV cache miss rate doubled, and the prefix cache wasn't warming as expected. I think the egress queueing to the NAT gateway lengthened requests.

[01:18] Marcus Leung: Just to add, our cloud team rotated a NAT gateway around 02:15 and there were a couple of transient SNAT port exhaustion alerts, could be related. I can share the metrics.

[01:40] Noah Green: SNAT exhaustion would definitely cause ephemeral connection stalls. For fallback routing, we have a policy that routes to the regional spare pool then to a compatible quantized model. There might be a subtle mismatch in model selection causing extra KV deserial work which extends latency.

[02:05] Ellen Park: When you say "compatible quantized model" can you remind me which variant we use in fallback? We want to make sure accuracy drift is acceptable.

[02:22] Jordan Kim: Good question — fallback goes to the redwood-3b-quant-lite variant for short bursts. For longer sequences we attempt to keep the same architecture; if not available we fall back to redwood-7b-quant which has a slightly higher token cost and sometimes a small latency delta. We logged some label inflation — transcription messed up a couple product names in the initial run, sorry about that.

[02:50] Priya Shah: No problem. The bigger issue is the 9% p95 regression on long prompts after the kernel upgrade — it was stable before. Marta, you looked into kernel 1.2.4?

[03:09] Marta Ruiz: Yeah, I ran the microbenchmarks. Kernel 1.2.4 introduced a new batching heuristic that reduces memory copies in the hot path but it also changes the continuous batching threshold, so for longer sequences we saw more cache churn. In our local repro the p95 went up ~8-12% for sequences over 1k tokens. We tried toggling the heuristic flag and saw p95 revert.

[03:45] Marcus Leung: Could that explain the night spike then? If batching behaves differently under burst conditions maybe queueing combined with SNAT made it worse.

[04:02] Marta Ruiz: Exactly. I suspect two compounding effects: network egress contention causing higher request durations and kernel batching pushing more work per batch leading to higher tail latency.

[04:27] Jordan Kim: Actionable path here — Marta can run a controlled test: rollback kernel to 1.2.3 and run the same traffic slice we saw last week, and then reapply 1.2.4 with the batching flag off. If we reproduce the spike only with 1.2.4 enabled, we'll propose shipping a small patch to disable the heuristic for BlueCrest's pool.

[04:58] Ellen Park: From an ops perspective, what's the cost and disruption of a rollback? We can't afford extended downtime.

[05:12] Noah Green: Rollback is non-disruptive if we do a canary: drain a single node from the dedicated pool, replace with 1.2.3 VM, redirect a % of traffic (5-10%) and measure. If health checks and SLOs hold we can roll the rest during low-traffic window. We'll provide runbook.

[05:38] Priya Shah: Sounds good. On security, BlueCrest compliance asked about KMS-integration for the private deployment. Do you have a recommended approach for key wrapping?

[05:52] Jordan Kim: Yes — we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM and yubikey HSMs in on-prem installs. We'll send the secure-arch diagram and the KMS key lifecycle notes. Marta, can you attach the sample kms-config yaml?

[06:12] Marta Ruiz: Yep, I'll include the sample and example encryption-at-rest config. Also note that audit logs are forwarded to your SIEM and are configurable for 90/365 day retention.

[06:30] Marcus Leung: On the ACL side, we want to confirm egress only to specific IP ranges. Would Redwood need additional firewall ports open?

[06:45] Noah Green: No additional inbound ports beyond the control plane. For egress we need outbound to Redwood's regional endpoints plus the selected cloud registry for model pulls. I'll send a minimal ACL list.

[07:05] Jordan Kim: Back to the experiments — Marta, can you summarize the actual numbers from last week's run? I want to capture them in the notes.

[07:15] Marta Ruiz: Sure. Baseline (pre-upgrade) for 1k-token prompts: p50 120ms, p95 340ms. After 1.2.4 upgrade: p50 130ms, p95 370ms — roughly 9% tail increase. The fallback routing success rate improved from 96.2% failures down to 1.3% failures, so availability tradeoff is net positive but tail latency hurt for long sequences. Also cost per token with fallback was +3.4% due to quantized model usage.

[07:48] Priya Shah: So availability improved dramatically, cost increased a bit, but tail latency is the main complaint. We'll need the breakdown by route and model variant.

[08:05] Marta Ruiz: I'll export route-level CSVs, including KV miss rate and cold-start counts. That should help correlating cache warmness.

[08:22] Marcus Leung: One tangent — have you considered prefix caching tweaks? We can keep a per-tenant small hot-cache pinned to reduce misses during bursts. That might improve p95 without kernel changes.

[08:35] Marta Ruiz: We did a small experiment with pinned prefix caches earlier; it reduces cold-start misses but increases memory footprint. On the Dedicated pool we can provision a slightly larger cache. Need BlueCrest signoff on memory tradeoff.

[08:52] Ellen Park: We're willing to allocate extra memory if it means better tail latency. What's the expected increase in footprint?

[09:02] Marta Ruiz: For our workload pattern, pinning the top 5k prefixes adds ~35% to model host memory usage per node. We can granularly pin only the top 1k and get most benefits with ~12% extra memory.

[09:20] Jordan Kim: Let's list a couple of parallel experiments: 1) kernel rollback canary, 2) pinned prefix cache to top 1k, 3) increase NAT pool / fix SNAT port exhaustion, 4) weekend soak with dedicated temporary pool. Each experiment should have clear metrics — p50/p95/p99, KV cache miss, fallback rate, and cost delta.

[09:58] Priya Shah: Agree. About the weekend soak — do you have capacity to spin up the temporary dedicated pool? If so what's the expected cost estimate?

[10:12] Noah Green: We can spin up a 2-node medium-gpu pool for a 48 hour soak. Estimate for that would be ~USD 1,200 as a one-off for the pilot. We will provide exact pricing in the follow-up.

[10:28] Marcus Leung: Can we also test the egress ACL changes in staging before the soak? We don't want NAT exhaustion to skew the results.

[10:40] Jordan Kim: Yes, do the egress ACL change first and validate with synthetic traffic. Marcus will coordinate with his cloud team.

[10:52] Priya Shah: On compliance, our legal asked if Redwood can sign a small amendment for encrypted logs at rest. Is that standard?

[11:04] Jordan Kim: We have addendum templates for encryption and retention. I'll loop in our security contacts and send the DPA addendum.

[11:16] Ellen Park: One last product question — the console dashboards. We need token-level cost breakdown per endpoint and route, is that available now?

[11:30] Marta Ruiz: Yes, the console has per-route and per-model cost slices. For private deployments some of the telemetry is shipped to your internal dashboard, but we can enable per-token tagging and billable metrics for the pilot.

[11:45] Priya Shah: Great. Anything else?

[11:52] Jordan Kim: Quick recap and owners: Marta runs the kernel rollback canary and the prefix-cache 1k experiment, Marcus will share egress ACLs and NAT metrics, Jordan will send security docs and the estimated soak pricing, Priya to confirm compliance contact. We'll reconvene after Marta posts bench csvs — propose a follow-up deep-dive on Friday 2025-10-10.

[12:18] (overlap / crosstalk) Marcus Leung: — I'll get the NAT metrics up, thanks.

[12:30] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone.

(End of transcript)

Notes: transcription includes a few mis-recognized terms (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache and "redwood-3b-quant-lite" was sometimes captured as "red-3q lite"). We left those in to reflect raw meeting export.
